schema_notes: Bean-editable. Add or modify models here; route.py re-reads on every call. v5 (2026-07-15): ALL-CLAUDE PURGE — cerebras, gemini-flash, gemini-pro, ollama-cloud, local-gemma4, local-qwen25 removed per Bean's no-non-Claude-models decision. Fleet is now haiku (cheap/mechanical, 200K ctx), sonnet (mid/architectural + large-context, 1M ctx), inline (main-thread Opus/Fable, never dispatched). Cross-PROVIDER QC became cross-TIER QC (reviewer = different Claude tier than author, cold context). CAPABILITY LOSSES documented: no offline/local tier (offline_required now flags-and-stays-inline); no free tier (cheap = Haiku). Sensitive content (secrets/PII) stays inline to minimise copies across subagent transcripts. v4 and earlier history: see git.
budget_thresholds_notes: Monthly cumulative spend ceilings in GBP. When exceeded (checked by scripts/check-budget.py), route.py activates 'budget_triggered' rules that step non-critical work down to Haiku until month end; critical (time_sensitivity=high) still routes normally. Inline (main thread) is never budget-gated.

haiku.reliability_notes: Anthropic API path, fast + cheapest tier. The mechanical workhorse: classification, extraction, formulaic edits, small well-scoped code gen.

sonnet.reliability_notes: Anthropic API path. 1M context window — absorbs the large-input/batch-synthesis role the old 1M-context models filled. Near-Opus quality on coding and agentic work. Supports MCP via Agent tool.

inline.command: (do not dispatch, handle in main conversation)
inline.reliability_notes: The current conversation — whatever frontier model the session runs on (Fable 5 as of 2026-07). Most expensive tier; the deep-reasoning role the old paid-credit 1M-context tier filled now lives here. Use when subagent isolation would break connected reasoning, for strategic work, and for sensitive content.

then.justification: Strategic work is inline by default per 2026-04-18 correction. Only qc_review and persona_panel task shapes may be delegated for this class of work — both have their own rules and both require report-back-inline.
No dispatch criterion met per 2026-04-15 subagent-dispatch-decision-rule. Inline wins for connected reasoning.

Content signal: credentials/secrets detected. All models are Anthropic now, but keeping secrets in the main thread minimises copies across subagent transcripts and logs. (The old local-model offline route was retired 2026-07-15 with the non-Claude purge.)

Content signal: PII detected. All providers are Anthropic (enterprise DPA), so no exclusion set is needed — but PII-bearing work stays in the main thread to minimise copies across subagent transcripts.
Content signal: jailbreak attempt suspected. Sonnet via Anthropic API has strong safety training + audit logging; keeps the suspect content out of the main thread.
MCP tools (Playwright, GitHub, etc) route via the Agent tool; Sonnet is the default MCP-capable dispatch tier (Haiku also supports MCP for simple fixed-shape calls).
Web search via /search skill in main thread; subagents can't invoke search.py reliably.
Destructive ops (DB migration, mass rewrite) need worktree isolation. Sonnet via Agent tool supports this.

CAPABILITY RETIRED 2026-07-15: the local/offline model tier (gemma/qwen via Ollama) was removed with the non-Claude purge. No Claude model runs offline. Work stays inline; if a genuine no-network constraint exists, flag it to Bean rather than dispatching.

Persona panel (brainstorming, gap-analysis rubric reviewers, research councils, critique pairs): breadth via parallel COLD Sonnet subagents, each primed with a distinct persona — independence now comes from cold context + divergent priming rather than provider diversity. Quality-first per Bean's philosophy; Haiku fallback (cap 8) when the panel is large and mechanical. Each persona reports back; main agent synthesises; findings surface inline with Bean before anything is applied.
Fast classification: Haiku optimised for this, Anthropic API is reliable, <3s latency.
Batch synthesis + large input: Sonnet's 1M context window fits large synthesis input. Escalate inline only when the synthesis is itself strategic.

inline.note: Main-thread Opus/Fable did the work — cross-check with a cold Sonnet reviewer (different tier + fresh context).

sonnet.note: Sonnet did the work — promote the review to the main-thread frontier model.

haiku.note: Haiku did the work — Sonnet reviews.

then.justification: QC must be cross-TIER (adapted 2026-07-15 from the 2026-04-18 cross-model rule when the non-Claude fleet was purged): the reviewer is a different Claude tier than the author, dispatched COLD so it shares no context with the authoring thread. Same-tier QC is rejected. route.py refuses to answer if original_model is not supplied.
Code review needs code understanding + multi-file reasoning; Sonnet is the spec-reviewer default per subagent-driven-development.

Content signal: high-complexity embedding (multi-hop reasoning, ambiguous requirements). Deep reasoning is the main-thread tier's job now that the old paid-credit deep-reasoning subagent tier is gone.
Small, well-scoped code gen fits the cheap tier; Haiku first. Fallback to Sonnet if the diff needs multi-file reasoning.
Input approaches Haiku's 200K-token context window; Sonnet's 1M window handles it.
Output exceeds the 8K-token self-imposed budget on Haiku dispatches (keep cheap-tier jobs small and verifiable).

Monthly Sonnet budget exceeded (per scripts/check-budget.py). Step non-critical work down to Haiku until month end; critical (time_sensitivity=high) still routes normally. There is no free tier in the all-Claude fleet — cheap means Haiku.

Default: reliable, 1M context, the right quality floor for unclassified dispatch work (quality-first per Bean's philosophy — higher-quality output means less human intervention). Mechanical shapes route to Haiku via higher-priority rules.
